summary: Jürgen Renn is a historian and philosopher who studied at Technische Universität Berlin and the Free University of Berlin (~1975–1982). He held posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (~1994), Free University of Berlin (~1995), and Humboldt University (~2006).

K. A. Subramania Iyer (1896–1992) was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who served as Professor at the University of Lucknow (attested 1972, 1987) and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Indologist K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer served as Secretary at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945) and as Managing Editor of the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras.

K. Kunjunni Raja (1920–2005) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned PhDs from the University of Madras (~1944–1947) under C. Kunhan Raja and London (~1951–1954) under John Brough, later holding posts at Madras (~1958–1980) and Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (~1981–2005).

K. Meenakshi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under Madhukar Anant Mehendale. She held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).
K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who served as Professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (attested 2008) and held a post at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020).

K. T. S. Sarao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Panjab University, the University of Delhi (BA to PhD, ~1973–1985), and Cambridge (PhD, 1985–1989). He taught at Kirori Mal College (1981) and Delhi (Professor, 1995).

K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director of the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986–1987) and Honorary Director of the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore (attested 2012).

K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Principal of Central Hindu College (~1935–1938) and Principal at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1937–1939).

K. V. Sarma (1919–2005) studied at the University of Kerala (~1937–1942) and worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He held positions at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (~1943–1951), University of Madras (1951–1962), and Sri Sarada Education Society (~1991–2005).

K. Venkata Ramanan, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at Peking University (1947–1949) under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang, and earned a DLitt from Visva-Bharati University, where he served as Professor of Philosophy.
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyu Mitomo and served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1900–1907). He held posts at Toyo University (~1908–1926) and Taisho University (~1926–1932).

Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at Keio and Komazawa. He lectured at Harvard (~1912–1913) and served as the first president of Komazawa University (1925–1934), alongside posts at Soto-shu University (~1925–1934).
Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served at Otani University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and professor (attested 1999–2002).
Kalikinkar Datta (1905–1982) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post at Patna University (~1930–1965), where he later served as Vice-Chancellor (attested 1973).

Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Palpung Monastery (~1918–1931) under Lama Norbu Dondrup, Khakyab Dorje, and Tai Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, later directing three-year retreats there (~1942–1955).
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi and served as a Professor at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).

Kamala Tiyavanich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there in 1993–1994.
Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) worked in Indology and philosophy, holding posts at Brown University (~1969–1970), the University of Toronto (~1970–1971), and the University of Bonn.
